messages.subject: Re: mirt rasch to winsteps
parts:
Does something like this help? https://philchalmers.github.io/mirt/html/Three-Rasch.html

Translation between software is indeed tricky, as even the estimators (MML vs CML) can make a difference in smaller samples.

Phil


On Thu, Aug 11, 2022 at 2:35 PM Chris Busath <jcbu...@gmail.com> wrote:
As a follow up, I found the functionality to adjust parameters in the model using the pars = "value" and then pars = adjustedpars. When I look at mine, it says that MEAN_1 = 0 as a default. However, when I average my difficulty parameters it is -1.68. If I adjust to MEAN_1 = 1.7, then the average of my difficulty parameters are 0.05. 

I was wondering if the scaling for parameter d had something to do with what I was seeing (https://embracingheterogeneity.github.io/website/01a_LR.html), however, I can't figure out why that would be the case since the d constant is only supposed to affect alpha not item location. 

Any thoughts?

On Wednesday, August 10, 2022 at 9:07:19 PM UTC-4 Chris Busath wrote:
Hello!

I work at a company that uses Winsteps to run rasch models. I would like to use mirt, but when I compare results (IRTpars = T) they are shifted (-1.68), though highly correlated. 

I read on the Winsteps website that meshing between software programs can be tricky (https://www.winsteps.com/winman/compatibility.htm), but it only gives advice on how to tune Winsteps results. Since I am a newcomer, I need to tune my results to what is already being used. 

I'm still relatively new to IRT, but I suspect this is a scaling issue. Is there an easy way to specify in the mirt function the slope (USCALE) or intercept (UIMEAN) like is suggested on the Winsteps page? Or is there a more appropriate solutions I should try?

Apologies if this is a repeated question. I did a brief search of previous conversations and nothing popped out.

Thanks!
Chris Busath
